extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, wire-service staff, and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service news dispatches covering Korean War developments, related domestic political/economic reactions, labor and security agreements, and explicit editorial instructions (Note to Editors) for handling sensitive military information. Contains both reporting and procedural guidance directed at editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-publication of national/state roundups of Guard/Reserve callups
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army requests that no publication be made of the roundup of National Guard units called to active duty which was carried on some wires in the day report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such compilations would be valuable to a foreign agent; it is urgently requested that no state or national roundup of mobilized National Guards or reserve units be undertaken by the wire services and those that have already been made be killed. Note: 'There is no legal restriction on such stories, the wire services...'. Governors have been asked to make future announcements only for local communities involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customary compliance with military security requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers and radio stations customarily abide by official requests when the question of military security is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although there may be no legal restriction, wire services and news outlets are expected to follow official urgings to withhold certain compilations or reports that could aid foreign agents or harm operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not list persons as bad security risks solely for union activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement provides that nobody is to be listed as a bad security risk because of union activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the maritime industry voluntary pact; while identifying security risks (e.g., Communist card-carrying, subversives) is a goal, being active in union activities alone should not be the basis for being labeled a bad security risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude known subversives/communist card-carrying seamen from ships
rubrics_metrics.description: Ship operators and workers recognized that certain men, because of being known as Communist Party card carriers, subversives, or who are notorious as consistently carrying out policies of the Communist Party, are bad security risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maritime statement asserts the goal of removing such security risks from American ships; the Coast Guard, Navy intelligence and FBI will assist in spotting suspected communist and subversive seamen. However the agreement also includes protections (replacements and appeals) for those rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ship delays; replacement and right of appeal for rejected seamen
rubrics_metrics.description: "No ship will be delayed because any such men are rejected" as bad security risks; signatory unions agreed to furnish a replacement for any man rejected as a security risk, and either the union or the employee affected will have the right of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational commitment: ensure vessel movements are not interrupted by removals; provide labor replacements promptly and establish appeal procedures at port and national levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coast Guard screening presence and interagency policing for crews
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the voluntary pact the Coast Guard will be in charge of the actual policing system; as a crew signs on each ship there will be a Coast Guard representative there to check them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policing system should operate quickly (statement: 'should be operating within a week') and will involve naval intelligence and the FBI to spot suspected communist and subversive seamen, similar to port security programs used in World War II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of port and national appeals boards for security decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A board is to be set up in each principal port, with over these there will be a national appeals board in Washington.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bodies will handle appeals from seamen or unions contesting security-related rejections; ensures a structured review process rather than unilateral listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep vessels sailing; resist obstructive demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: All signatory unions will 'keep the vessel sailing' should any non-signing organization try to delay or obstruct ship movements by such things as phony demonstrations and bogus picket lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatories pledged operational solidarity to prevent delays caused by protest tactics; news reporting may note this pledge as part of maritime policy to maintain logistics during the emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note-to-editors practice for sensitive military information
rubrics_metrics.description: AP includes editorial notices (e.g., 'NOTE TO EDITORS') instructing member newspapers and wire services about handling sensitive security-related material (what to publish/kill).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms receiving such notes are expected to follow standing guidance and to treat official requests to withhold or kill stories about mobilization or other security matters with deference, even where no legal prohibition exists.
